messages:
Mae (Customer): Hey team, customer C-3456 reports intermittent failures on streaming responses. Most requests succeed but ~1 in 10 ends with a gateway 502 or client error 'connection reset by peer' during the stream. They say client sees partial chunks then a broken pipe.

Liz (Support): Thanks Mae. Can you paste the request-id and any logs they gave? Also which SDK/version?

Mae (Customer): Request-id: r-8f3b2a0. SDK: official-js v2.4.1. Customer log: `stream closed, err=ECONNRESET, retrying...` They also attached our gateway log snippet: ```
[2026-03-14T14:02:11Z] r-8f3b2a0 upstream_timeout=0 downstream_err=ECONNRESET status=502 path=/v1/stream
[2026-03-14T14:02:11Z] r-8f3b2a0 upstream_resp_time_ms=120 node=gw-03
```

Liz (Support): Copying Omar and Jordan. Omar, can you take a look at the gateway mapping? This is getting counted as 5xx and tripping the customer's SLA alarm.

Omar (SRE): On it. First pass: that log line shows downstream (client) connection reset but status=502. We probably treat any non-2xx path as backend failure. Need to see the gateway source mapping for chunked responses.

Omar (SRE): Quick grep: ```
$ grep r-8f3b2a0 /var/log/gateway/gw-03.log | tail -n 20
[...]
[2026-03-14T14:02:11Z] r-8f3b2a0 chunk_stream: first_chunk_sent=true keepalive=60 downstream_err=ECONNRESET mapped_status=502
```

Jordan (Oncall): We've seen similar post-deploy last week when the streaming proxy started closing sockets aggressively for idle streams. Two hypotheses: (1) client-side aborts mid-stream get mapped to 5xx, (2) chunk framing issue causes the proxy to reset the TCP connection.

Liz (Support): Mae, can you reproduce reliably? Any small repro snippet we can give SRE?

Mae (Customer): I can repro locally. Steps: `curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=small\"` then Ctrl-C after a few chunks. Client sees `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection was reset`. The gateway logs map it to 502.

Omar (SRE): Repro is great. I put together a quick test harness that simulates an abrupt client close: ```bash
# start streaming request in background
curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" "${API}/v1/stream?model=toy" > /tmp/stream.out &
PID=$!
# wait for first chunk then kill connection
sleep 0.8
kill -9 $PID
# check gateway logs for the request id
```

Omar (SRE): Root cause: gateway's streaming proxy treats ECONNRESET from downstream as an upstream error if the request had already started, and increments the `requests.5xx` counter. For user-initiated aborts we should map to a client-abort category (499) and not count as server error. Also we saw a regression where final-chunk timeout was being double-counted.

Jordan (Oncall): Agreed. Mitigation options: (A) fast rollback of the recent proxy change, (B) hotfix that maps downstream RST/FIN to 499 and excludes from SLA 5xx metric, (C) update SDK guidance to retry with backoff and idempotency tokens for streaming endpoints. I vote B as the fastest with least blast radius.

Omar (SRE): I'll open a small patch on the gateway: detect socket errors where `errno==ECONNRESET || errno==EPIPE` coming from downstream and, if we've already flushed at least one chunk to the client, mark the request as `client_abort` and emit `http_status:499` and `metric:requests.client_abort`. Also add a defensive check: if mapped_status==502 && downstream_err in (ECONNRESET,EPIPE) then decrement requests.5xx. Patch snippet: ```diff
--- a/proxy/streaming.go
+++ b/proxy/streaming.go
@@ -420,6 +420,12 @@ func handleDownstreamErr(err error) {
-    metrics.Incr("requests.5xx")
-    resp.Status = 502
+    if isClientReset(err) {
+        metrics.Incr("requests.client_abort")
+        resp.Status = 499
+        // don't count as server 5xx
+        return
+    }
+    metrics.Incr("requests.5xx")
 }
 
 func isClientReset(err error) bool {
     // EPIPE/ECONNRESET from downstream
 }
```

Liz (Support): ETA for hotfix? Also Jordan, can we do canary first?

Jordan (Oncall): Yes canary on gw-canary-1 first. Omar, please include a feature flag to toggle mapping so we can flip quickly.

Omar (SRE): Will do. Patch + unit tests + canary deploy in ~90m. I'll also add a small metric `requests.client_abort` and update dashboards so it doesn't leak into 5xx alarms.

Mae (Customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please let me know once canary is up so I can hit canary endpoint to verify.

Omar (SRE): Canaries up: gw-canary-1. To test against canary, use header `X-Gateway-Canary: gw-canary-1` or host header `gw-canary-1.api.redwood.example`. Repro steps same as before.

Mae (Customer): Tested against canary: I aborted after 2 chunks, client saw close but dashboard shows `status=499` and 5xx metric unchanged. Nice. Still see occasional 502s (~1/200).

Jordan (Oncall): That residual 502 might be the root framing bug I mentioned. Omar, can you triage whether those 1/200 are from chunk framing vs tcp resets?

Omar (SRE): Investigating. Found a second class: when the client sends a FIN exactly as server writes last chunk, proxy occasionally misparses content-length/chunk boundaries and raises protocol error -> 502. Hotfix v1 handles client aborts but not this race. I'll add an additional tolerant parser for last-chunk framing where we accept a clean FIN as success rather than protocol error.

Omar (SRE): Pushed v2 to canary that treats EOF after chunk termination as OK. Deploying to canary now.

deploy-bot: deploy/gateway-hotfix v1.2.3 -> canary completed (gw-canary-1) :rocket:

ops-bot: alert muted for SLA-5xx for customer C-3456 during investigation (owner: @Jordan)

Omar (SRE): Canary v2 looks good. Running soak: 10k streaming requests, previously failure rate 0.9%, now 0.02%. Preparing prod rollout in 30m.

deploy-bot: deploy/gateway-hotfix v1.2.3 -> prod started

Jordan (Oncall): Prod rollout complete. Metrics: `requests.5xx` for C-3456 dropped from 12/hr -> 0-1/hr. `requests.client_abort` shows expected volume ~8/hr.

Liz (Support): Mae, can you confirm with your customer that their alarms are quiet and the SDK logs show `client_abort` mapping?

Mae (Customer): Confirmed. Customer reports no more flaky SLA alerts. They still see client-side `Recv failure: Connection was reset` when they abort manually (expected) but no backend 502. :white_check_mark: Thanks all.

Jordan (Oncall): Postmortem: will write short postmortem and link to followup PR for better chunk framing tests and add a synthetic test in canary to kill client after first chunk. Assign to Omar and eng-runtime.

Liz (Support): Closing thread after postmortem published. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
